title: Hyper-Dimensional Fingerprints as Molecular Representations
abstract: arXiv:2604.27810v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Numerical molecular representations underpin virtual screening, property prediction, and materials discovery. Conventional fingerprints are efficient and deterministic but lose structural information through hash-based compression at low dimensionalities, whereas graph neural networks recover expressiveness through compute-intensive, task-specific training. Here, we introduce hyperdimensional fingerprints (HDF), which compose the chemical attributes of atoms and their multi-hop environments through algebraic operations on high-dimensional vectors, producing deterministic representations without any training. Across diverse property-prediction benchmarks, HDF ranks consistently among the best representations across datasets and models. Crucially, HDF encodes structure more efficiently: at low dimensionalities, its distances correlate with graph edit distance more strongly than Morgan fingerprints', yielding effective similarity metric

translated_title: 超维指纹作为分子表示
translated_abstract: 数值化分子表示是虚拟筛选、性质预测和材料发现的基础。传统指纹方法高效且具有确定性，但在低维度下会因基于哈希的压缩而丢失结构信息；而图神经网络虽能恢复表达能力，却需要计算密集、针对特定任务的训练。本文提出了超维指纹（HDF），通过对高维向量进行代数运算来组合原子的化学属性及其多跳环境信息，无需任何训练即可生成确定性的分子表示。在多种性质预测基准测试中，HDF在各个数据集和模型上均始终位列最佳表示方法之列。至关重要的是，HDF能更高效地编码分子结构：在低维度下，其距离与图编辑距离的相关性比Morgan指纹更强，从而提供了有效的相似性度量。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无需训练的超维指纹（HDF），通过高维向量代数运算组合原子化学属性与多跳环境信息，生成确定性分子表示，在性质预测基准上表现优异，且在低维度下比传统指纹更高效地编码分子结构。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces hyperdimensional fingerprints (HDF), a training-free molecular representation that composes atomic chemical attributes and multi-hop environments through algebraic operations on high-dimensional vectors, achieving top performance across property prediction benchmarks and encoding structure more efficiently than conventional fingerprints at low dimensionalities.
